title: Closed direct image commutes with simultaneous strict derived reduction
statement:
Let $\ell$ be a prime, $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ a finite extension, $R=\mathcal O_E$ its valuation ring, $t$ a uniformizer and $A_n=R/t^n$ for $n\ge1$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ be a closed immersion of schemes with quasi-compact open complement $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-closed-immersion, def-weil-open-immersion, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Use the small pro-etale sites, constant finite coefficient sheaves and completed coefficients $B_T=\varprojlim_n(A_n)_T$ for $T=X,Z$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf, def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients], with the canonical identification $i^{-1}B_X\cong B_Z$ and the finite projections of [lem-weil-pbc-profinite-coefficient-inverse-image]. Use ordinary unbounded module derived categories [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let $\mathsf S_A(T)$ be the category of strict systems of $(A_n)_T$-module sheaves with semilinear quotient transitions and levelwise exactness [lem-pur-coefficient-system-derived-comparison]. Write $I:D(\mathsf S_A(Z))\to D(\mathsf S_A(X))$ for termwise closed direct image, induced by its exact sheaf functor [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-ringed-open-closed]. Let $\mathcal R_T:D(B_T)\to D(\mathsf S_A(T))$ be simultaneous derived reduction, computed from one flat-term K-flat resolution by $(P\otimes_{B_T}(A_n)_T)_n$, with transitions $1\otimes q_{n+1,n}$ [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image, def-weil-integral-reduction-tower].

There is a canonical natural isomorphism of actual derived systems
$$r_P:\mathcal R_X(i_*P)\xrightarrow{\sim}I\mathcal R_Z(P)\qquad(P\in D(B_Z)).$$
Its evaluation at $n$ is the canonical closed projection comparison
$$(i_*P)\otimes^L_{B_X}(A_n)_X\xrightarrow{\sim}i_*(P\otimes^L_{B_Z}(A_n)_Z).$$
Before deriving, the projection map on sections is the sheafification of $s\otimes a\mapsto s\otimes i^{-1}a$. The comparison $r$ is its derived comparison in the category of systems; it commutes with all quotient transitions and with the quotient augmentation from the constant $B_X$-module tower $\Delta_Xi_*P$, after restriction of scalars to $B_X$. These are equations of transformations of derived systems. No constructibility, completeness or boundedness is assumed, and no lifting of a family of maps from the individual derived categories is part of the assertion.

source.place: Integral-stage closed counit reduction: agent-extracted simultaneous comparison obligation. Exactness input: Stacks Tag 09BM, proetale.tex, lemma-closed-immersion-complement-retrocompact-exact; the tag does not itself assert the strict-system projection comparison.

proof.text: Identify $i^{-1}B_X=B_Z$ and $i^{-1}(A_n)_X=(A_n)_Z$ by the canonical coefficient comparisons; these identifications commute with every projection and quotient map. Write $p=i^{-1}$ and $q=i_*$ over these coefficients. The closed and open inverse images are exact, $q$ is exact, and the closed counit $pq\to1$ is invertible: the ringed closed-kernel adjoint statement, for an arbitrary commutative ring sheaf and a quasi-compact open complement, says that the ordinary termwise closed counit gives $i^*i_*\cong1$. Apply the specified exact derived adjunction to obtain $p\dashv q$ on unbounded derived categories, with the localized original unit $\eta$ and counit $\varepsilon$. Apply the same ordinary constructions levelwise to strict systems: the adjunction equations hold levelwise, since inverse image, direct image, unit and counit are natural for the semilinear transitions. Exactness is levelwise, so this gives exact termwise functors on systems and their derived categories. No assertion about commuting a nonexact right derived functor with evaluation is required.

source.place: Integral stage, closed counit reduction; agent construction on strict systems using the closed adjunction and flat-term K-flat localization.

proof.text:
For a flat-term K-flat complex $Q$ of $B_X$-modules, put $T_X(Q)_n=Q\otimes_{B_X}(A_n)_X$. There is a natural cochain map
$$u_{Q,n}:Q\otimes(A_n)_X\xrightarrow{\eta}q p(Q\otimes(A_n)_X)\xrightarrow{q\sigma}q(pQ\otimes(A_n)_Z).$$
Here $\sigma$ is the ordinary inverse-image tensor isomorphism followed by the canonical coefficient identification. The degree-$a$ section formula on a local pure tensor is $x\otimes b\mapsto\eta_Q(x)\otimes i^{-1}b$, interpreted as a section of the direct image; it follows from the unit's tensor normalization. This balanced bilinear formula respects restriction and hence sheafification. Naturality in $Q$ shows commutation with the differential, which is $d_Q\otimes1$, and with chain maps. A chain homotopy $h$ is carried to $h\otimes1$, so the maps are defined on the homotopy category as well.

source.place: Integral stage, closed counit reduction; agent construction on strict systems using the closed adjunction and flat-term K-flat localization.

proof.text: The maps of Step 2 form one strict-system map $u_Q:T_X(Q)\to qT_Z(pQ)$. Indeed, for $m\ge n$, both paths around its transition square send $x\otimes b$ to $\eta_Q(x)\otimes q_{m,n}(i^{-1}b)$; the other expression is $\eta_Q(x)\otimes i^{-1}(q_{m,n}b)$ and these agree by the coefficient comparison. Equality on local pure tensors implies equality after sheafification. Before forgetting the level coefficient action the map is $(A_n)_X$-linear, since multiplication by $a$ sends either expression to $\eta_Q(x)\otimes i^{-1}(ab)$. After restriction to $B_X$, the two paths from $\Delta_XQ$ to $qT_Z(pQ)$ agree: both send $x$ to $\eta_Q(x)\otimes1$. Here the paths use respectively the quotient augmentation of $T_X(Q)$ and the unit followed by $q$ of the quotient augmentation of $T_Z(pQ)$. These are equations of maps of strict complexes, not just evaluated derived equations.

source.place: Integral stage, closed counit reduction; agent construction on strict systems using the closed adjunction and flat-term K-flat localization.

proof.text:
Descend this construction through the full homotopy subcategory $\mathcal P_{B_X}$ of flat-term K-flat complexes. It localizes to $D(B_X)$ by the resolving-subcategory equivalence. For $Q\in\mathcal P_{B_X}$, $pQ$ is flat-term K-flat by the ringed-topos pullback theorem. For any quasi-isomorphism between such $Q$'s, tensor with each $(A_n)_X$ preserves that quasi-isomorphism; the same holds after $p$ and after exact $q$. Thus both system-valued functors in $u_Q$ invert those quasi-isomorphisms, since system cohomology is levelwise. The localization universal property descends the natural transformation, giving
$$u_M:\mathcal R_X(M)\longrightarrow I\mathcal R_Z(pM)\quad(M\in D(B_X)).$$
The factorization isomorphisms are the K-flat computations specified in the statement: this identifies the descended functors with the specified $\mathcal R_X$ and $I\mathcal R_Zp$. The same universal property descends the augmentation square of Step 3 to the derived category of strict $B_X$-module towers; scalar forgetting and the constant diagram are exact levelwise. Uniqueness gives independence of resolutions and naturality on all derived morphisms.

source.place: Integral stage, closed counit reduction; agent construction on strict systems using the closed adjunction and flat-term K-flat localization.

proof.text:
For $P\in D(B_Z)$ define
$$r_P=I\mathcal R_Z(\varepsilon_P)\circ u_{qP}:\mathcal R_X(qP)\longrightarrow I\mathcal R_Z(P).$$
This is already a natural transformation with target the derived category of actual strict systems. Its evaluation is the canonical derived closed projection comparison: before deriving, for a sheaf $N$ on $Z$, the composite of Step 2 with $q(\varepsilon_N\otimes1)$ sends $s\otimes a$ to $s\otimes i^{-1}a$. Equivalently its $p\dashv q$-transpose is $(\varepsilon_N\otimes1)\sigma$, precisely the characterization of the ordinary closed projection map. These identities are natural in complexes and descend by Step 4, so evaluation gives the derived comparison for the specified change-of-rings functors, including its $(A_n)_X$-module structure.

source.place: Integral stage, closed counit reduction; agent construction on strict systems using the closed adjunction and flat-term K-flat localization.

proof.text: Fix $n$ and view $e_nr_P$ as a morphism of $(A_n)_X$-module derived objects. Its closed restriction is an isomorphism: derived inverse image commutes with derived tensor, and $pqP\xrightarrow{\varepsilon_P}P$ is invertible, being the localization of the termwise closed counit, which is invertible by the ringed closed-kernel adjoint statement; the triangle identity identifies the restricted map with the resulting tensor identification. Its open restriction is an isomorphism between zero objects. Indeed $j^{-1}qP=0$, and the derived tensor pullback formula gives $j^{-1}(qP\otimes^L_{B_X}(A_n)_X)=0$; the target is a closed direct image and also restricts to zero. Exact inverse images commute with cohomology. Hence the cohomology sheaves of the cone of $e_nr_P$ have zero open and closed restrictions. Open/closed zero detection, applied with ring $(A_n)_X$, makes every one of these sheaves zero. Thus the cone is acyclic and $e_nr_P$ is invertible. This uses neither a Tor bound on $P$ nor flatness of $(A_n)_X$.

source.place: Integral stage, closed counit reduction; agent construction on strict systems using the closed adjunction and flat-term K-flat localization.

proof.text: Let $C$ be the cone of $r_P$ in the derived category of systems. Exact evaluation gives $H^a(e_nC)=0$ for all $a,n$ by Step 6. Since kernels, cokernels and exactness in the strict-system category are levelwise, each system $H^a(C)$ has every component zero and is zero. Consequently $C=0$ and $r_P$ is an isomorphism of actual derived systems. Its transition compatibility is already part of its construction as a system map; this argument uses evaluation only to test invertibility.

source.place: Integral stage, closed counit reduction; agent construction on strict systems using the closed adjunction and flat-term K-flat localization.

proof.text:
Write $a_T:\Delta_T\to\operatorname{Res}\mathcal R_T$ for the quotient augmentation. The descended equation of Step 3 is $u_M a_X(M)=q a_Z(pM)\,\Delta_X\eta_M$. With $M=qP$, compose it with $q\operatorname{Res}\mathcal R_Z(\varepsilon_P)$. Naturality of $a_Z$ changes the result to $q a_Z(P)\,\Delta_X(q\varepsilon_P\circ\eta_{qP})=q a_Z(P)$, by the adjunction triangle identity. Therefore
$$\operatorname{Res}(r_P)\,a_X(qP)=q a_Z(P),$$
under the canonical equality $\Delta_XqP=q\Delta_ZP$. The equation was obtained from strict-complex equations by faithful localization precomposition, so is an equation of transformations into the derived category of strict $B_X$-towers. Together with Steps 3 and 5 this proves every transition, evaluation and augmentation clause of the statement.
